text:
Alex Kim: Quick question — am I eligible for the short-term childcare reimbursement while I'm on a 60% phased return next month? Trying to figure out if we can cover a backup nanny for mornings only.

Maria (People Ops): Hi Alex — short answer: maybe. Longer: eligibility depends on hire date, active benefits enrollment, and the subsidy policy cap. Part-time phased returns are prorated. :memo:

Alex Kim: Cool. What docs do you need? I have invoices and a payment screenshot. Also curious if we can backdate to last month when I had to pay out of pocket.

Olivia (Benefits): Hi — we need the vendor invoice (company name + service dates), proof of payment (bank/credit screenshot), and a short note from manager confirming need/coverage dates. For backdating, we can approve up to 60 days retro by exception; longer requires exec sign-off.

Jamal (Eng Manager): I can write the manager note — I'll confirm the coverage dates and that Alex was on team-approved phased return. Ping me when you have the dates. :white_check_mark:

Maria (People Ops): Policy highlights: max $1,200 total per 6-month period (pro-rated for part-time). If you were on 60% FTE, the cap is 60% of the full amount unless there's an extraordinary exception. International note: non-US payouts may need local tax treatment — payroll will flag that.

Alex Kim: Thanks. For receipts, is this format ok?
```
Vendor: Sunny Days Nanny Co.
Service: backup nanny mornings
Dates: 2026-04-05 to 2026-04-30
Amount: $480
Payment: Bank transfer 2026-04-05 (ref 1234)
```

Olivia (Benefits): Yep — perfect. Please upload all docs to the benefits portal case (Benefits > Reimbursements > New request) and tag it "short-term childcare". In the case description include the phased-return % and manager note filename.

Payroll Bot: FYI — international employees: reimbursement will be processed via payroll code CHRMB on next off-cycle if submitted before cutoff (15th). Otherwise, next regular payroll.

Alex Kim: One last — can we split reimbursement across two pay cycles if amount > cap for that month?

Maria (People Ops): We can split payments in payroll, yes. If you expect totals to cross multiple pay periods, mention preferred schedule in the case. We'll confirm timeline once docs are in.

Alex Kim: Submitted the case and uploaded everything, case #CHR-4572. Thanks everyone. :pray:

Olivia (Benefits): Received. I'll route to payroll and flag for international tax review. Expect a confirmation reply within 2 business days.

Payroll Bot: Case CHR-4572 acknowledged. Estimated processing: payment on 2026-05-20 (or earlier if off-cycle approved).

Jamal (Eng Manager): Thanks — happy to help with any follow-up notes.

Alex Kim: Appreciate it.
